newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers slump again, buyers play waiting game.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers slump again, buyers play waiting game.

text.p: ARA bunkers slumped, prices in other European ports mostly fell further on Thursday and buyers patiently waited for the market to bottom out, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil was down by about $2 a tonne to around $107/108 fob as healthy availability in the barge market caused prices to slump for the second consecutive day. Lack of bunker deals added to the sense of oversupply.
A number of enquiries emerged, including one for 3,000 tonnes, in the morning, but few deals materialised by the close.
"The buyers seem to think there'll be more price decreases and why not if the market is so poor," one dealer said.
Hamburg bunker losses were even more extreme than in ARA as the market took into account the two-day ARA slump. Prices for 380 CST were at around $119 fob.
As in ARA, deals were thin on the ground.
Mediterranean ports presented a mixed bag of prices, some, such as in Spain, steady, others, as in southern France, were up to $4 lower. Few ports registered healthy demand.
Fujairah bunkers were down by about $4 a tonne with buyers, as elsewhere, sitting out.
